title: Mind the Generation Process: Fine-Grained Confidence Estimation During LLM Generation
one_line_claim: FineCE provides fine-grained confidence scores throughout LLM generation by training on probabilistic response distributions and using backward confidence integration from subsequently generated tokens.
method_summary: FineCE trains a supervised model on generation sequences using a pipeline that captures probabilistic response distributions. Employs Backward Confidence Integration to leverage information from subsequently generated text to improve confidence estimates for earlier sequences. Three position optimization strategies identify where confidence assessment should occur.

key_findings.finding: FineCE delivers fine-grained confidence scores at multiple points during text generation.
key_findings.quote: existing approaches suffer from coarse-grained scoring mechanisms that fail to provide fine-grained, continuous confidence estimates throughout the generation process

key_findings.finding: FineCE consistently outperforms existing classical confidence estimation methods across multiple benchmarks.
key_findings.quote: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that FineCE consistently outperforms existing classical confidence estimation methods

key_findings.finding: Addresses LLM tendency toward overconfidence and lack of self-awareness when making predictions.
key_findings.quote: addresses a critical limitation in large language models -- their tendency to be overconfident and lack self-awareness when making predictions

relation_to_herald.shared: Both operate during text generation and aim to detect quality degradation. Both work with per-token signals and provide early warnings during generation.
differs_on: FineCE estimates confidence for any sequence; HERALD specifically targets compression-induced catastrophic failures using XGBoost on logit features.
FineCE optimizes confidence positioning; HERALD predicts failure onset H tokens ahead with a fixed temporal horizon.
FineCE is a general confidence estimation tool; HERALD is task-specific for predicting looping and non-termination in KV-cache compressed settings.
